title: COMP 4537 · Lecture 4
subtitle: Servers and Node.js: what a server is, PHP's four steps against Node's three, the restaurant analogy, modules with require and exports, the http, url and fs built-in modules
description: Lecture 4 of Amir Amintabar's COMP 4537: a server as a computer running 24/7 reachable over the internet, the client / web server / DB server / file server / mail server figure, what a server-side script can do, Node.js as an open-source cross-platform JavaScript runtime on Chrome V8, how PHP or ASP handles a file request in four steps and Node.js in three, the restaurant analogy (one non-blocking waiter, one blocking waiter, one waiter per table) and the 100-requests-100-threads figure; then VS Code debugging, the area examples and their wrong formulas, a math.js module loaded with require('./modules/math'), the http server with createServer, writeHead(200, ...), write, end and listen(8888), Access-Control-Allow-Origin, url.parse(adr, true) with host, pathname, search and query, the ?name=John server, and the fs file server with its 404 branch. A playback of the three restaurants and of a request passing through createServer's callback; every Node listing pinned with the output the slide shows. Ends with a 20-item mock quiz in the shape of Quiz 7.
intro:
:::quiz Midterm weight
The midterm is 30 % of the course and covers lectures 1 to 6 in full plus lecture 7's Node-to-MySQL part, so this lecture carries roughly a sixth of the exam's multiple-choice and short-answer marks. It also supplies the Node half of the coding questions: writing a small `http` server that reads a query string, returns HTML with `writeHead(200, ...)`, and answers 404 for a missing file. Quiz 7 drew six of its ten items from these slides. Closed book except one letter-sized double-sided sheet, so the PHP-vs-Node steps, the restaurant mapping and the `url.parse` fields must come from memory or the sheet.
:::
